subject.title: [Feature] Decouple dreaming from memory-core — allow any memory plugin to implement dreaming protocol

question: Should OpenClaw add an OpenClaw-managed memory dreaming provider protocol, or keep dreaming orchestration plugin-owned/ClawHub-only until memory role slots land?
rationale: The remaining work adds public plugin SDK, config, scheduler, artifact, and migration semantics, and current related PRs show multiple plausible API shapes that automation should not choose.

options.title: Coordinate provider protocol with role slots
options.body: Keep this issue open, use PR #88504 as the role-slot foundation if accepted, then design the dreaming-specific provider lifecycle and contract on top of it.

options.title: Define a standalone provider protocol now
options.body: Proceed with a dedicated MemoryDreamingProvider design independent of role slots, but require SDK/docs/baseline/compatibility tests and real alternate-plugin proof before implementation lands.

options.title: Keep dreaming plugin-owned
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide OpenClaw core should not own generic dreaming orchestration and ClawHub plugins should provide vector-native dreaming independently.

recommendation.title: Coordinate provider protocol with role slots
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, use PR #88504 as the role-slot foundation if accepted, then design the dreaming-specific provider lifecycle and contract on top of it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about core public plugin/config API direction and repository governance identifies steipete as the project decision owner.
